newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refined copper output rose in Jan from Dec.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refined copper output rose in Jan from Dec.

text.p: U.S. refined copper production rose to 220,700 short tons in January compared to 212,000 short tons in December, the American Bureau of Metal Statistics said.
Refined copper production outside the U.S. in January was 945,700 short tons, down from 954,100 short tons in December.

Shipments from U.S. refiners in January totaled 204,400 short tons, compared with 198,100 short tons in December. Total U.S. shipments in January and December, were 204,400 and 206,200 short tons respectively.
Refinery based copper inventory in January in the U.S. totaled 14,000 short tons, compared with 16,500 short tons in December.
Total world refined copper inventories in January, including metal at plants and in exchange warehouses, were 348,400 short tons, down from 353,000 short tons in December.
Total world shipments in 1996 was a revised 13,778,200 short tons.
